clips.title: DjangoCon 2021 | Speed up your tests with setUpTestData | Adam Johnson
clips.why: A Django core contributor opens his talk on why the speed of a test suite matters to the people (and now the agents) who wait for it.
look: Why a slow suite changes how often people run it at all.
Where the time in a Django test run usually goes: setup, not the asserts.
The idea of doing expensive setup once and sharing it, which is what our template does for the database.
clips.after: Nova reruns the API layer after every edit, so a few seconds saved per run is minutes saved per ticket.

clips.title: Re-Write Django tests with pytest | pytest fixtures & test functions
clips.why: Shows pytest-django's client fixture and the pytest.ini that tells pytest which Django settings to load, the two pieces every tests_api test stands on.
look: The client fixture sends a request into Django without a server, like our APIClient.
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE in the pytest configuration: without it pytest-django cannot start Django.
How the test reads the response's status code and content.
clips.after: tests_api has its own pytest.ini for the same reason, so it does not pick up the integration tests' settings and markers.

clips.title: What are Template Databases in PostgreSQL | A deep dive
clips.why: Every CREATE DATABASE in Postgres already copies a template; this part shows that default.
look: CREATE DATABASE copies template1 when you do not name a template.
The new database starts with everything the template had.
Why that makes a template a fast way to start many identical databases.
clips.after: Our conftest names its own template, migrated once, instead of the empty template1.

clips.title: How to Use a Custom Template Database in PostgreSQL
clips.why: The whole trick in about a minute: build a database once, then create new ones from it with TEMPLATE.
look: CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE with your own database as the source.
The copy has the tables and rows of the source at once.
The rule that nobody may be connected to the source while it is copied.
clips.after: That last rule is why our conftest closes every Django connection before the workers copy the template.

practice.q: A teammate writes a test that calls one method on the Project model, with no request. Where does it go?

options.text: tests_api, because new tests use pytest.
options.why: The split is by kind of test, not by age. tests_api is for tests that call an endpoint and check the response.

options.text: rhinoCore/tests, next to the other model and service unit tests.
options.why: A test of one model method or service stays where those tests live; nobody moves old tests in bulk.

options.text: The integration tests, so it runs on QA.
options.why: A model method needs no real environment. QA is the slow, shared answer the new layer exists to avoid.

practice.q: Finish the line that gives a worker its own copy of the template.
practice.hint: One Postgres keyword that names the source database.
practice.why: CREATE DATABASE new TEMPLATE old copies the files of old on disk, so no migration runs.

practice.q: pytest-django builds the test database in a session fixture. What name must your conftest's fixture have to replace it?
practice.hint: Three words joined by underscores, starting with django.
practice.why: A fixture in conftest.py with the same name as a plugin's fixture wins, so pytest-django uses ours.

practice.q: Put the first run with the template in order, with four workers on a fresh Postgres.
items: All four workers ask for advisory lock 7007; one gets it, three wait
The first worker finds no template, creates it and runs every migration into it
It closes all its connections and copies the template into test_app_gw0, then releases the lock
The next worker gets the lock, finds the template and only copies it
Each worker's tests run in its own copy, each test in a transaction that is rolled back
practice.why: Only one worker ever migrates. Everyone else waits a moment and copies, and the tests run fully in parallel afterwards.

practice.q: An agent edits a JSON fixture file that the template loads, then runs only the affected tests with testmon. What is the risk?

options.text: testmon runs every test, so it is only slow.
options.why: testmon runs fewer tests, not more. That is the risk here.

options.text: testmon sees no Python code change and may run nothing, while the template may also still hold the old rows.
options.why: Setup files are invisible to testmon, so a change there must run the whole layer, and the file must be part of the template's name.

options.text: pytest-django refuses to load fixtures under xdist.
options.why: Fixtures load fine; the template loads them once before the copies.

practice.q: Without connections.close_all(), the copy fails with "source database is being accessed by other users". Who is the other user?

options.text: Another CI job using the same Postgres.
options.why: The lab and each CI job have their own Postgres; the culprit is inside this run.

options.text: The worker itself: Django kept the connection it used to run the migrations into the template.
options.why: Postgres only copies a database nobody is connected to, so we close Django's connections before CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE.

options.text: The test database of worker gw0.
options.why: A copy is a separate database; being connected to it does not block copying the template.
